review_evidence: Reviewed the 28 primary lean-subst files. The project explicitly formalizes De Bruijn substitution infrastructure inspired by Autosubst, including heterogeneous simultaneous substitutions, renaming embeddings and automation laws.
The hydrated source contains 315 proposition declarations and 548 declaration-style items, including substitution/renaming composition, lifting and extensionality results.
The theorem-bearing substitution metatheory is reusable formal-semantics prior art and remains retained.
summary: Reviewed lean-subst and retain its extensive theorem-bearing De Bruijn substitution and renaming metatheory.

review_evidence: Per-file non-comment line counts (lines not blank and not starting with --): Archive/LambdaCalc.lean 4 of 115, Archive/LambdaCalcKit.lean 3 of 138, Archive/SystemF.lean 4 of 388, Archive/SystemF2.lean 4 of 182; no '/-' block comments in any Archive file.

Top-level declaration grep (theorem|lemma|def|inductive|structure|class|instance|abbrev at line start) gives 0 for all four Archive files; LeanSubst/Ops.lean 198, Examples/SystemFCallByValue/Term.lean 170, LeanSubst/Automation/Basic.lean 102, LeanSubst/Class.lean 75, LeanSubst/Laws.lean 44.

rules.content_invariant: A format-aware check (every line other than import/open/namespace/end starts with `--`, and no `/-` block comments exist) shows the files declare nothing; the commented text describes abandoned hand-written lambda-calculus and System F renaming/substitution instances whose live counterparts are in LeanSubst/ and the Examples term files generated by #leansubst.
evidence: Archive/LambdaCalc.lean: read all 115 lines; live lines are import LeanSubst, open LeanSubst, namespace/end Examples.LambdaCalc; Term inductive, from_action, rmap, smap, ren_*/subst_* theorems and SubstMap* instances are all commented.

Archive/LambdaCalcKit.lean: read all 138 lines; live lines are import LeanSubst and namespace/end LeanSubst.Examples.LambdaCalc; Term, Kit class, kitmap, ren/subst theorems and instances are all commented.

Archive/SystemF.lean: read all 388 lines; live lines are import, open, namespace/end Examples.SystemF; Ty/Term inductives, Ty setup, Term setup and ListRen experiments are all commented (some doubly).

Archive/SystemF2.lean: read all 182 lines; live lines are import, open, namespace/end Examples.SystemF2; Ty/Term inductives, Ty.rmap/smap, Term.rmap/smap and RenVecMap/SubstVecMap instances are all commented.
rules.rationale: Each Archive file is a fully commented-out draft: outside `--` line comments it contains only `import LeanSubst`, optionally `open LeanSubst`, and an empty `namespace ... end` pair. Lean elaborates no declaration, statement, or proof from these files, so hits on them would point search at declarations that do not exist.

summary: Surveyed all 33 unit files across Archive/, Examples/ and LeanSubst/ with ls, wc -l, per-file non-comment line counts, block-comment counts, and top-level declaration counts. Read in full the four Archive files, the six Examples import aggregators, Examples.lean, LeanSubst/Glue.lean, and the non-comment content of Examples/STLC/Term.lean, Examples/SystemFWithNat/Term.lean and LeanSubst/Automation/Attributes.lean. The four Archive files contain only `import LeanSubst`, `open LeanSubst`, and an empty namespace; every definition, theorem and instance in them is inside `--` line comments, so Lean elaborates no declaration from them. They are excluded. All other files stay searchable: the LeanSubst library files and the Examples term/theory files hold live De Bruijn renaming and substitution definitions, laws, rewriting and normalization theorems, and #leansubst generation commands; the Examples/*.lean aggregators contain only imports but stay primary-eligible under FILTER-007.
